s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral lower limb weakness and pain with signs of inflammation and nerve paralysis following unaccustomed physical activity
key_facts: Unipolar major depression with psychotic features
Completed a 5 km flat walk the evening prior to symptom onset
Presented to the emergency department three days later
Visibly swollen and reddish colored legs

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral lower limb weakness and pain with signs of inflammation and nerve paralysis following unaccustomed physical activity
key_facts: Unipolar major depression with psychotic features
Completed a 5 km flat walk the evening prior to symptom onset
Presented to the emergency department three days later
Visibly swollen and reddish colored legs

shortlist.label: Compartment syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral peroneal nerve paralysis, hardened painful forelegs, and swollen legs suggest increased pressure within muscle compartments

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CPK (15,000U/L) and muscle edema on MRI indicate muscle damage and necrosis

shortlist.label: Exertional myositis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent unaccustomed physical activity (5 km walk) and muscle edema on MRI support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe pain, swelling, and signs of inflammation (CRP: 280mg/dL, WBC: 25,000/μL) raise concern for this condition

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Painful swelling and hardened forelegs, along with elevated inflammatory markers, make this a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral foot drop, painful swelling of the legs, hardened painful forelegs, and visibly swollen and reddish colored legs, along with the laboratory findings of elevated CPK and imaging studies showing indirect signs of myositis and panniculitis, are consistent with compartment syndrome. The recent unusual physical exertion of a 5 km walk may have triggered the condition.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated CPK, the presence of bilateral peroneal nerve paralysis and the imaging findings are more suggestive of compartment syndrome than rhabdomyolysis alone.

rejected.label: Exertional myositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are more severe than what is typically seen in exertional myositis, and the imaging studies suggest a more complex condition.

rejected.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
rejected.why: The patient's temperature is only slightly elevated, and there is no clear evidence of necrotizing fasciitis on the imaging studies.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not suggest eosinophilic fasciitis, which is typically characterized by a distinct clinical and histological presentation.
